meta.disclaimer: Educational clinical reference only — not a prescription. For pulpal/periapical pain and localized swelling in an otherwise healthy patient, the treatment is DEFINITIVE DENTAL TREATMENT (e.g., pulpotomy, pulpectomy, non-surgical root canal, or incision & drainage), not antibiotics. Antibiotics are added only with systemic involvement (fever/malaise) or high risk of spread. Verify doses against the current source and local formulary.
meta.notes: US adult figures from ADA 2019 (Lockhart et al.). US paediatric dosing from AAPD 'Useful Medications'. UK figures from SDCEP (Bacterial Infections, updated May 2026) and NICE/UKHSA. Metronidazole: avoid with warfarin; avoid alcohol during and 48h after. Co-amoxiclav is usually unnecessary.

recommendation.summary: Do NOT prescribe antibiotics. Provide definitive conservative dental treatment (pulpotomy, pulpectomy, non-surgical root canal, or incision & drainage) and manage pain with analgesics.

rules.rationale: Antibiotics provide negligible benefit and potentially large harms for these conditions in healthy adults without systemic involvement; definitive dental treatment resolves the source.
rules.source_locator: Recommendations against antibiotics; good practice statements.

recommendation.summary: With systemic involvement (fever/malaise): amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily for 3–7 days, OR penicillin V 500 mg four times daily for 3–7 days — alongside definitive dental treatment. Re-evaluate at 3 days.

cautions: reassess at ~3 days; discontinue 24h after symptoms resolve
antibiotics are an adjunct to, not a substitute for, definitive treatment
rules.rationale: Antibiotics are indicated when systemic signs are present or the risk of progression is high.

recommendation.summary: Penicillin allergy without anaphylaxis/angioedema/urticaria: cephalexin 500 mg four times daily for 3–7 days.

rules.rationale: Cephalexin is an option for non-severe penicillin allergy.

recommendation.summary: Severe penicillin allergy: azithromycin 500 mg day 1 then 250 mg once daily for 4 days (ADA 2019 preferred). ADA 2019 also lists clindamycin; because of C. difficile risk, clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily is a common stewardship alternative.

options.label: Clindamycin (ADA 2019 alternative)
options.notes: Guideline-listed alternative; weigh Clostridioides difficile risk. Confirm dose against the source.

options.label: Clarithromycin (stewardship alternative)
options.notes: Often preferred over clindamycin for lower C. difficile risk.

recommendation.notes: ADA 2019 lists azithromycin or clindamycin for severe penicillin allergy; clarithromycin is shown as a stewardship-oriented substitution.

rules.rationale: Macrolides are the alternative when penicillin allergy is severe; clindamycin is de-emphasised due to C. difficile risk.

population.notes: Children < 40 kg use weight-based dosing; >= 40 kg use adult dosing.

recommendation.summary: Children with systemic involvement, alongside definitive treatment: amoxicillin 20–40 mg/kg/day divided every 8 hours (or 25–45 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours); ≥40 kg use adult dosing. Penicillin-allergic: azithromycin (weight-based) or, if needed, clindamycin per specialist advice.

components.dose: 20–40 mg/kg/day divided q8h (or 25–45 mg/kg/day divided q12h)

cautions: definitive dental treatment remains the priority
rules.rationale: Paediatric therapeutic dosing per AAPD, applied only when systemic involvement is present.

recommendation.summary: Do NOT prescribe antibiotics for localized dental infection without spreading/systemic signs. Provide dental treatment (drainage/extirpation/extraction) and analgesia.

rules.rationale: SDCEP/NICE: antibiotics are not indicated for localized infection amenable to dental treatment; overuse drives resistance.
rules.source_locator: SDCEP dental abscess management; NICE CKS.

recommendation.summary: If antibiotics are indicated (spreading infection / systemic signs), alongside dental treatment: amoxicillin 500 mg three times daily, OR phenoxymethylpenicillin 500 mg–1 g four times daily, for up to 5 days; review at 3 days. Add metronidazole 400 mg three times daily for spreading infection or pyrexia. For severe infection the dose may be doubled.

options.label: Metronidazole (adjunct for spreading infection/pyrexia)
options.notes: Avoid with warfarin; avoid alcohol during and for 48h after.

cautions: amoxicillin reserved where penicillin V compliance is difficult (stewardship)
rules.rationale: SDCEP/NICE first-line agents and durations for dental infection requiring antibiotics.

recommendation.summary: Penicillin allergy: clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily, OR metronidazole 400 mg three times daily, for up to 5 days; review at 3 days.
